name: Vathakuzhambu
ingredients: Sundakkai vathal (dried turkey berry) or Manathakkali vathal
Sambar powder or red chili powder and coriander powder
instructions: 1. Soak a lemon-sized ball of tamarind in warm water and extract the juice.
2. Heat gingelly oil in a pan and fry the vathal (dried berries) until crisp, then set aside.
3. In the same oil, add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, and curry leaves.
4. Sauté chopped shallots and garlic until golden brown.
5. Pour in the tamarind extract, add turmeric powder, salt, and sambar powder, and let it boil until the raw smell disappears.
6. Add the fried vathal and a small piece of jaggery to balance the acidity.
7. Simmer until the gravy thickens and oil separates from the sides, then serve with steamed rice.
description: Vathakuzhambu is a traditional staple of Tamil Brahmin cuisine, known for its long shelf life and medicinal properties. It is typically prepared as a comforting meal for long journeys or on days when one wants to enjoy a deeply flavorful, tangy gravy that aids digestion.
